1541	## 13. CLI reference
1542	
1543	Every command prints what it produced first, then a one-line outcome (✓ or
1544	✗), and its problems last: diagnostics, errors and warnings with their help
1545	and notes, then the error and warning count. On a terminal the output is
1546	coloured and paths are marked `+`/`-`; piped or with `NO_COLOR`, it is plain
1547	text and stdout carries the bare results.
1548	
1549	| Command | Behaviour |
1550	| --- | --- |
1551	| `piton check [paths...]` | Validates syntax, imports, references, types, inheritance, composition, exports and circular dependencies, reporting errors and warnings. Writes nothing. Exits 0 when there are no errors and 1 otherwise. Paths are optional files, directories or globs; the default is the project (or every `.pi` file under the working directory when there's no `piton.config.pi`). |
1552	| `piton build [config] [--dry-run]` | Builds the project configured by `piton.config.pi` (or the given config). Writes renderer output to `<output>/<path under root>.<ext>` (defaults: `./dist`, JSON), so `spec/components/Button.pi` becomes `dist/components/Button.json`: the entry file plus every file holding something the entry's exports reference. A registered framework's output replaces it unless the config sets `output` or `renderer`, which asks for both. Records every file in `.piton/manifest.json`. The whole plan is validated before anything is written. `--dry-run` reports without writing. |
1553	| `piton compile <path> [--renderer json\|yaml\|markdown] [--write] [--dependencies]` | Compiles one file to stdout (JSON by default): one key per export. `--write` writes `<file>.<ext>` next to each input and is required for globs. `--dependencies` wraps the result as `{"value": "<compiled output as a string>", "dependencies": [absolute source paths]}` so build tools know what to watch; bundled package files are left out. |
1554	| `piton format [path] [--check]` | Applies canonical formatting (4-space indents, constraint spacing, sorted and wrapped imports, no `.pi` in import paths, a space after `//`). `--check` reports without writing. `piton format -` reads source from stdin and writes the formatted text to stdout. It **only splits overflowing lines and never rejoins a paragraph**, so rewrap edited prose by hand, and don't reflow `key: value` blocks as prose. |
1555	| `piton reach [targets...] [--no-unreachable] [--no-paths]` | Starting from files, globs or anchor names (the entry by default), follows outgoing imports, references, inheritance and composition, direct and transitive. Reports what is reachable with its depth and the path taken, and what is unreachable. The flags hide the last two. Use it to find dead spec. Grouped by source, with a summary. No diagnostics; always exits 0. |
1556	| `piton slice <target> [--adapter <target>]` | Prints the part of the spec one thing depends on, as one Markdown document for an agent's prompt. The target is `file.pi#Anchor`, `file.pi#Anchor.property`, `file.pi#variable`, or a bare name looked up across the project (an error when more than one file declares it). Follows, transitively: what an anchor extends, every base that also declares a property, anchors named by type constraints, what a value read (`${Other.x}`, variables), and what it references or embeds. Imports alone bring nothing in. A whole anchor needs all its properties and bases; slicing a property leaves out the anchor's other properties; a reference to a property needs only that property. It also includes the **chain** from the project's entry down to the target (`Specification.Tooling`, `Tooling.cli`, `Cli.commands`): the shortest path the build takes, each link only that one property and not followed further. An export of the entry, a variable, and a file the build doesn't reach have no chain. Order: the target, then its dependencies nearest first (source order breaks ties), then the chain outermost first, so the same source prints the same bytes. Each declaration appears once, headed by its name as written (`SaveButton.color`), with its file, what it extends, its type and what it reads. References and embeds are written as names; cycles are followed until they come back around. Every path it prints is relative to the directory it runs in, and it finds the project by looking upward for `piton.config.pi`. `--adapter claude-code` (any Belay target the project builds) cites the compiled output instead: each location and every reference links to where `piton build` writes it (an embedded anchor to the section that embeds it), and no `.pi` file is ever cited; an abstract base or an anchor that is only read has no document of its own and is described without one. With `--adapter` the target itself must be something the build writes out. Markdown links the author wrote pass through unchanged. Exits 1 on errors. |
1557	| `piton init [directory] [--template <group/name>] [--adapter <id>...] [--list]` | Starts a new project from a template compiled into the compiler (no network needed). Templates come in groups: `piton/minimal` (plain Piton to JSON), `piton/library` (a package others can tether), `belay/application` (a shape instruction placed in `src/`, a skill, an agent and a command) and `belay/minimal` (the Belay config and one skill). Without a directory it first asks for the project's name and creates that directory (an empty answer, or no terminal, uses the working one). Then it asks for a group and a template (`--template belay` asks only for the template), and for a Belay template, which adapters to build for: a checklist of Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode with the template's default (Claude Code) checked, or `--adapter`, repeated or comma-separated. The chosen adapters replace the config's import and `adapters` list, and a template's `.adapters/<id>/` files (like OpenCode's `opencode.json`) are written only for the adapters chosen. Templates are the `group/name` directories in the compiler repo's `create-templates/`, each with a one-line `.template` description that is not written out; adding one is adding a directory, and every template must check cleanly, be formatted, and build. `--list` describes the groups and templates and does nothing else. With no terminal, a full template name is required. It never overwrites a file: if any it would write exists, it names each and writes none, and cancelling a question writes nothing. Prints each written path on stdout, then a summary and the next commands on stderr. Exits 1 on errors. |
1558	| `piton loc [paths...]` | Counts total, code, comment and blank lines per file, with a summary. Defaults to the project. No diagnostics; always exits 0. |
1559	| `piton lsp` | Runs the language server over stdio (section 14). |
1560	| `piton agent [claude] [--print-fluency] [args...]` | Launches the agent with a short project primer plus this fluency prompt (the project's `FLUENCY_PROMPT.md`, or the copy built into the compiler), passed to `claude` as `--append-system-prompt`. Extra arguments go to the agent. `--print-fluency` prints the prompt and does nothing else. |
1561	| `piton tether [source] [--as name]` | See section 12. |
1562	| `piton update [packages...] [--force] [--diff]` | See section 12. |
1563	| `piton untether <package> [--as name] [--no-rewrite]` | See section 12. |
1564	| `piton remove <package>` | See section 12. |
1565	
1566	Each CLI command in the spec is a `cli-command` anchor
1567	(`spec/scope/tooling/cli/index.pi`) with `commandName`, `positionalArguments`
1568	and `namedArguments`.
1569	
1570	## 14. Language server, editors, and JavaScript
1571	
1572	`piton lsp` provides, from the spec's feature list:
1573	
1574	- Diagnostics (not for missing optional properties), completion, hover (type,
1575	  source, documentation, inheritance chain, export status and compiled
1576	  interpretation), go-to-definition, find-references, and rename across the
1577	  whole specbase.
1578	- Auto-import, import organization, and code actions: import a missing
1579	  symbol, create an unresolved anchor, add an export, qualify an ambiguous
1580	  reference, resolve a simple inheritance conflict.
1581	- Document and workspace symbols, semantic highlighting, inlay hints
1582	  (resolved types, inherited origins, composition sources), formatting,
1583	  folding and selection ranges.
1584	- Inheritance, composition (`+`, `++`), override and conflict resolution;
1585	  reference resolution; validation and type information for expressions in
1586	  `{}`, `${}`, `#{}` and `@{}`; export validation; module resolution; cycle
1587	  detection (circular imports are fine and not reported).
1588	- Related-symbol navigation, a hierarchy view, resolved-value and provenance
1589	  inspection, compiled-output preview, source-to-output mapping, unused and
1590	  redundant definition detection, and documentation integration.
1591	- Incremental analysis and workspace indexing.
1592	- Diagnostics cover Belay semantics as well as Piton. Import organization
1593	  flags unused, duplicate, invalid and overly broad imports. Cycle detection
1594	  also catches an anchor that ends up extending itself, and shows the cycle.
1595	
1596	There is no signature help.
1597	
1598	Completion rules: never suggest things that don't exist; offer nothing on an
1599	empty value (`property: `), because prose probably follows; offer nothing
1600	after a `.` inside a string.
1601	
1602	Editing rules every editor must follow, through the LSP or the editor
1603	extension:
1604	
1605	- Enter after a colon that opens a dictionary or anchor property starts a new
1606	  line indented one level deeper.
1607	- Enter on a blank line inside a dictionary or anchor starts a new line one
1608	  level shallower.
1609	- Format-on-save is optional. It adds the space after `//` and touches nothing
1610	  else that is commented.
1611	
1612	Supported editors and their highlighters (spec): VS Code (TextMate plus LSP);
1613	Emacs, Helix and Zed (tree-sitter plus LSP); Neovim and Vim (vim syntax);
1614	JetBrains (`jetbrains`); Sublime (sublime-syntax); Kate (KSyntaxHighlighting).
1615	Every editor gets full LSP support. The integrations live under `editors/`.
1616	
1617	**Consuming Piton from JavaScript.** `packages/vite-plugin-piton` imports
1618	`.pi` files as modules, with HMR, dependency tracking (through
1619	`piton compile --dependencies`) and virtual modules. Each export in the Piton
1620	file is a named export, and the default export is the whole file, the same as
1621	`piton compile` gives:
1622	
1623	```ts
1624	import { SaveButton } from '../spec/app.pi';
1625	import spec from '../spec/app.pi';
1626	
1627	const button = SaveButton;
1628	const cancel = spec.CancelButton;
1629	```
1630	
1631	It has a configurable default renderer (`renderer: 'json' | 'yaml' |
1632	'markdown'`), and the renderers can also be imported as functions
1633	(`vite-plugin-piton/renderers`) and used inline. `packages/astro-piton` is an
1634	Astro integration that wraps the Vite plugin.
1635	
1636	## 15. Working on a specbase
1637	
1638	1. **Orient.** Open `piton.config.pi` to find `root`, `entry`, `output`, the
1639	   frameworks, the adapters, `codeRoot` and `shapeRoot`. Read the entry file,
1640	   usually `spec/index.pi`, because its exports are the compilation roots.
1641	   Follow the `index.pi` files down through the modules. In this repository,
1642	   `spec/index.pi` exports `Specification` (FoundingThesis, Language, Tooling,
1643	   Belay, PackageManagement) plus the skills and command in `spec/agent/`.
1644	2. **Read compiled reference for overview, and source for truth.**
1645	   `<referenceRoot>/**/*.md` is easy to browse, and its links are lazy, so
1646	   follow them only when relevant.
1647	3. **Edit the `.pi` source**, following the conventions around it:
1648	   - one exported anchor per file, named after the file;
1649	   - `index.pi` files that re-export with `from ./X export *`;
1650	   - abstract anchors exported with a keyword, and shared abstracts in a
1651	     `lib/` folder;
1652	   - lowerCamelCase property names;
1653	   - SCREAMING_CASE for exported constant lists;
1654	   - prose in string blocks, and structure in keys and lists;
1655	   - `@{X}` to link related documents;
1656	   - examples inside fences wrapped in a `\\\` escape block.
1657	4. **Keep imports honest.** Use `use` for keywords and `from ... import` for
1658	   names; a file often needs both. A new file only compiles if the entry
1659	   reaches it, so export it through an index or reference it.
1660	5. **Validate.**
1661	   - Run `piton check`.
1662	   - `piton check` does **not** compile the examples inside escape blocks
1663	     (they are literal text). When you edit spec examples, extract each ` ```piton ` block,
1664	     run `piton compile` on it, and compare with any ` ```json ` block that
1665	     follows. Remember that compile output has only exported names.
1666	   - Run `piton build`, then look at the diff of the generated files.
1667	   - Run `piton reach` to confirm new anchors are reached.
1668	   - Run `piton format --check`.
1669	6. **Never hand-edit generated files.** That includes `CLAUDE.md` and
1670	   `AGENTS.md` under `codeRoot`, everything under `.claude/`, `.codex/`,
1671	   `.agents/`, `.opencode/` and the build output directory that is listed in
1672	   `.piton/manifest.json`, and the files in `.piton/` themselves.
1673	7. **Keep implementation and spec in agreement.** The implementation is judged
1674	   against the spec. When they disagree, report it instead of quietly bending
1675	   the spec to fit. Trust `piton compile` for how things behave today, and
1676	   flag the gap.
1677	
1678	## 16. Where the compiler differs from the spec
1679	
1680	Checked with `piton compile` and `piton build`:
1681	
1682	- The CLI has a few things the spec doesn't name: `build --dry-run`,
1683	  `tether --as`, agent argument passthrough, the `reach` flags, and
1684	  `format` with no path or `-`.
1685	
1686	- **Paragraph breaks.** The spec says a blank line in a string block starts a
1687	  new paragraph. The compiler joins the paragraphs with a single `\n`, which
1688	  Markdown output renders as one paragraph with a soft line break.
1689	
1690	Known limitations, where the spec is silent and the compiler's choice may
1691	surprise you:
1692	
1693	- A `/`-rooted import inside an installed package resolves against the
1694	  consuming project's root, not the package's. Use relative imports inside a
1695	  package.
1696	- A required property from an abstract is not satisfied by a value inherited
1697	  from a concrete base (`needs Thing extends Base`, where `Base` supplies it):
1698	  the keyword's anchor comes last, and its value-less declaration wins. Give
1699	  the value on the anchor itself.
1700	- `piton check` with no paths checks what the entry reaches, so a file that
1701	  nothing imports is not checked. Name it: `piton check path/to/file.pi`.
1702	- **Prose directly in an anchor body is silently dropped.** `anchor A:` with
1703	  only a line of text under it (no key) compiles to an empty anchor, with no
1704	  diagnostic. Always put prose under a key, such as `description:`.
1705	- Mixed-type equality is simply unequal: `{1 == "1"}` is `false`, not an
1706	  error. The spec says `==` works on every type but doesn't spell this out.
1707	- Which constructs each adapter requires a `description` for (section 11.2)
1708	  is hardcoded in `crates/piton-belay/src/adapter.rs`, not declared in the
1709	  adapter `.pi` files.
